solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make Ada rice when mixing sponge

indicators.note: mixing stirs these three words together, so their letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A baking instruction: tell Ada to make some rice while the mixer is going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mixing' is the anagram signal on MAKE ADA RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira cake is a classic plain British sponge, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Organised criminals intend rising about a fine

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the following letters
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: to intend is to aim
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Gangsters planning a heist end up with a fine instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AIM into MIA, and 'about' wraps that around A and F.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is the best-known organised crime syndicate, a gang of criminals working as a body.

clue.text: Finish with a draught for a decisive ending

parts.note: death is the finish of a life
a draught of air is a blow, as when the wind blows

explanation.surface: Someone ends an evening with a drink, choosing that draught to settle matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draught' looks like a drink, but here it is a current of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathblow is the stroke that settles a fight once and for all, so figuratively any decisive ending.

clue.text: Rice with carp, never right for a cold area

indicators.note: never right says no R is allowed anywhere, so every R goes from the words

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right; both of them go here

explanation.surface: A recipe for rice and carp that somehow never turns out right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never right' strips the R from both RICE and CARP, leaving ICE and CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice over polar land, a region that is always frozen.

clue.text: Electrical discharge in large vessel reported

indicators.note: reported means the word is as heard when spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Noah's ark was a large boat

explanation.surface: A news item: a spark of electricity aboard a big ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a luminous electric discharge jumping across a gap, as in arc welding.

clue.text: Look over alcohol where there are duty-free shops

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Checking out the drinks in a shop where alcohol is sold tax-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look over' reads as a phrase meaning inspect; split it, since 'over' is only the down-clue signal for placing one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty-free shops are found in airport departure lounges, so the definition describes the place.

clue.text: Daring to come in with pressure increasing

parts.note: to come in is to enter
P is the physics symbol for pressure
something increasing is rising

explanation.surface: It takes nerve to walk in when the pressure keeps mounting.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising people show bold initiative, so it is a synonym of daring in the sense of venturesome.

clue.text: A great sight — robins, say, compete in English tree

parts.note: robins are an example of birds, flagged by say

indicators.note: in puts the competing word inside the tree

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: A wonderful scene of robins fighting it out in an English tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A great sight' pun: an overall view from high above, as a bird sees things.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's-eye view is a panoramic view from above, which takes in a great sweep of sight.

clue.text: Get angry if invaded by northern poor

indicators.note: invaded by means the word if has another letter forced inside it

parts.note: a poor excuse is a lame one

explanation.surface: A northern incursion sparks anger among the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame can mean to become heated or provoked, which is to grow furious.

clue.text: Wagon broken by a weight of stones

indicators.note: broken by means the wagon word is split open with the next piece inside

parts.note: a cart is a wagon

explanation.surface: A wagon collapses under a load of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stones' suggests rocks in the cart, but here means gemstones, weighed in carats.
explanation.definitionFit: The carat is the unit for weighing gemstones such as diamonds, 200 milligrams.

clue.text: Paid back low newspaper interrupting Her Majesty's division

indicators.note: back means the word paid is written from end to start
interrupting means one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: HM is the abbreviation for Her Majesty, as in HM Treasury
a rag is a disreputable tabloid paper

explanation.surface: A tabloid repaid after meddling in a royal government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal and 'interrupting' the insertion signal; 'division' means a dividing wall in the body, not a government department.
explanation.definitionFit: The diaphragm is a partition, the muscular sheet dividing chest from abdomen.

clue.text: Hostile West African country gets biting insect around November

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: around means the insect word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting fly
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An unfriendly West African state is plagued by biting insects in November.
explanation.definitionFit: Malignant means full of ill will, actively intending harm, much like an enemy.

clue.text: Obviously, all rowers need this to start

definitions.text: Obviously, all rowers need this to start

indicators.note: to start asks for the starting letter of each of the opening words

explanation.surface: A truism: every rower plainly needs one of these to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes the first letters of Obviously, all, rowers; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Every rower must have a blade to pull through the water, so the clue describes the answer as rowing equipment.

clue.text: Preserve tree invaded by many blessed ants initially

indicators.note: invaded by means the tree word has the following letters forced inside

parts.note: the elm is a tree
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
B is the abbreviation for blessed, as for a beatified person

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word ants

explanation.surface: A tree is overrun by a swarm of holy ants.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to treat it chemically so that it is kept from decay.

clue.text: Thief left food all over car that hasn't started

indicators.note: all over means turned over, so the food word is read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: a car that hasn't started is missing its starting letter

explanation.surface: A thief has left food scattered over a car that won't start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' looks like scattering but is the reversal signal; 'that hasn't started' drops the first letter; 'left' is a letter, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is a criminal who breaks into buildings to steal.

clue.text: Bad result for part of Ireland

indicators.note: bad means the letters of the word result are spoiled into a different order

explanation.surface: A poor outcome for one region of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, which includes Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Inherited pub at end of lane

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the word lane

explanation.surface: Someone has inherited a pub at the far end of a country lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn, passed down at birth rather than acquired.

clue.text: Organ the archbishop has installed

indicators.note: has installed says the phrase the archbishop holds the answer inside it, set within the words

explanation.surface: A church has had a new organ put in by its archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests church music, but here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the organ of hearing, part of the body.

clue.text: Swig ales wildly holding new drinking vessel

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled letters contain the next piece
wildly says the letters of swig ales are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down beer recklessly from a fresh glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' jumbles SWIG ALES; 'holding' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wineglass is a stemmed glass for drinking wine, a type of vessel for drinking.

clue.text: Tree's more bare with top removed

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: balder means more bare, with less hair

explanation.surface: A tree in winter is growing steadily barer.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family, often found by water.

clue.text: I had clerk starting late and finishing early — layabout

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: starting late and finishing early means the word clerk loses its opening and closing letters

explanation.surface: A boss complains about a clerk who came in late and left early: a shirker.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone who avoids work and lazes around, the same as a layabout.

clue.text: Staff perhaps travelled on bicycles mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: to ride a bicycle, past tense rode

explanation.surface: Employees probably cycled to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick, as 'perhaps' warns.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a stick or pole, and a rod is one example of such a pole.

clue.text: Leave a group playing

parts.note: a band is a musical group
something playing is on, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A band walks off stage mid-performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or go away from, so it is a synonym of leave as a verb.

clue.text: Violently rebel toward someone widely seen as leader

indicators.note: violently means the letters of rebel toward are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel lashes out at a person everyone regards as the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A world-beater is someone who is the best anywhere, the acknowledged champion of their field.
